THE PROBLEM

Help to move shouldn’t hurt — or cost a fortune

102K–115K
QAR per year

for a hired caregiver plus physiotherapy for one bedridden client (the third card; ≈ US$28K–$32K a year).

Older adult. Joint pain in feet, shoulders and fingers; blood feels stuck in her feet. Cost today: low.
Family caregiver. Cares for a relative who can’t stand or walk alone. Care costs about QAR 4,092 a month (≈ QAR 49K a year).
Professional caregiver. Her bedridden client has fibromyalgia, so touch hurt; she wore soft gloves. Care costs QAR 102K–115K a year.

Today’s options fall short: workarounds hurt or depend on others, and robotic devices cost $399+ a month (≈ QAR 1,450) or are 18 kg clinic machines. This supports UN SDG 3 (good health for all ages) and Qatar National Vision 2030. In Qatar, the UN projects people aged 60+ growing from 103,000 in 2020 to 782,000 in 2050, more than seven times as many.

WHAT MOVA DOES

A wearable that moves the joint for you, set from your phone

The device moves the joint gently inside safe preset limits, so no hands-on touch is needed. Set the range, speed and session time in the app, and track progress after every session. In our analysis of H Robotics, CYBERDYNE and Motus Nova, none fully offers phone-app control of every movement setting.

The wearable (simulation). Straps, two circuit modules and a gear at the elbow. Concept simulation — not a prototype.
The app (mockup). 1 Set, 2 Move, 3 Track. Concept mockup with sample data — not a prototype.

MOVA aims to support blood flow by keeping the joint moving. It measures motion, not blood flow, so a pilot would test that claim.

WHO IT HELPS
Older adults
Daily tasks with less stiffness.
People with disabilities
Keeps joints moving; aims to support blood flow.
After an accident or surgery
Guided, gentle movement while recovering.
Adults with joint problems
Gentle stretching, no forceful help.
Family and professional caregivers
Helps without painful touch or heavy lifting.

= $294

Each device costs about $325 (parts and assembly), lasts about 3 years and serves about 2.25 rental customers. Selling a device at $849 gives a 48% gross margin, so rental is our lead model. The 6-month minimum rental protects us: a 6-month rental loses about $48. All costs are team estimates from our pricing model, not supplier quotes. QAR at 3.64 per USD.
